title: Harden filter visual oracles: assert filter pixels render in Ruffle (regression guard for 1238)
description:
REGRESSION PREVENTION tied directly to the confirmed CRITICAL defect task 1238 (PlaceObject3 HasFilterList bit was wrong, so ALL filters were silently dropped at runtime in Ruffle). Per AGENTS.md this is a legitimate test task — it is tied to a real, observed critical bug, not speculative coverage breadth.

PROBLEM: the pre-existing filter visual oracles in apps/desktop/e2e/visual-oracle.spec.ts are too weak to catch filters being dropped:
  - 'blur filter renders non-blank in Ruffle' (~line 852): asserts only `nonWhitePixels > 100`.
  - 'glow filter renders non-blank in Ruffle' (~line 973): same non-blank-only assertion.
  - 'bevel filter renders non-blank in Ruffle' (~line 1103): same.
  - 'drop shadow filter renders consistently' (~line 773): compares vs the EDITOR render at a loose `mismatchRatio < 0.20`.
A plain unfiltered rect is also non-blank (passes >100), and a 20% editor-diff tolerance is far too loose. These oracles passed for the ENTIRE project history while filters were silently dropped at runtime — they did not catch task 1238. That is the exact failure mode CLAUDE.md warns about: 'byte-presence is not runtime proof' and 'blank-white screenshots are ambiguous'.

PROPOSAL: replace the non-blank assertion with a per-filter-type Ruffle render assertion that COUNTS filter-produced pixels OUTSIDE the unfiltered shape's bounding box, compared against a no-filter control rendered identically:
  - Publish two SWFs: one with the filter, one identical but with filters removed (the control).
  - Screenshot both in Ruffle, then count lit/colored pixels in a region strictly OUTSIDE the source shape's bounds (where only a halo/shadow/glow can appear).
  - Assert the filtered render has materially MORE such pixels than the control (which should have ~0 there).
This was proven to work during the 1238 verification: a yellow Glow produced ~4792 lit halo pixels outside the shape vs 0 for the no-filter control. Apply the same outside-bounds delta technique per filter type (blur: softened/spread edge pixels beyond the crisp control edge; glow: colored halo; bevel: highlight/shadow on opposing edges; drop-shadow: offset shadow pixels in the offset direction with ~0 in the control). Keep the threshold well above noise but comfortably below the observed signal.

REFERENCE: task 1238 (HasFilterList bit fix, commit 14243fc). Also consider extending the suite to cover the shape filter+blend case from the sibling task (1240-5ehpxt) once that is fixed, so a dropped blend on a filtered shape is also caught.

NOTE: visual-oracle e2e is intentionally CI-skipped today (Ruffle WASM infra not wired in CI per CLAUDE.md); the hardened assertions run locally via `pnpm --filter @flash/desktop e2e`. Acceptance: each hardened test FAILS when the filter is dropped (verify by temporarily reverting the 1238 fix or stubbing the filter list to empty) and PASSES with filters intact.
